title: AHU-1 · basement hydronic air handler
text: AHU-1 · basement hydronic air handler Confirmed Model / part Lennox AM30Q2/3-70-2 Location Basement · left of Polaris tanks Role in the system Receives its own heating branch from the elbow beyond the two supply tees. An internal Taco pumps water through the heating coil; the blower transfers heat to air. The coil returns to the common heating return near the left Polaris. The MABS equipment connection is inferred, not traced end to end. Serial 5898M07675 · 120 V · water inlet maximum 180 °F. Internal pump Taco 006-B4-11. Separate cooling coil C26-41-1, serial 6099H46722, HCFC-22; its 450 psi rating is refrigerant-side, not water pressure. Duct distribution is outside this guide’s scope. title: Room thermostats & staging
text: Room thermostats & staging Staging unverified Model / part Living Area: Nest Thermostat (app: 1st generation); other models unrecorded Location Living Area, Master Bedroom, upstairs rooms, basement; separate Master Bath control Role in the system Owner describes radiant as first-stage heat and forced air as supplemental stage 2. The exact relay/staging wiring has not been fully traced. The homeowner expects stage 1 to stay on with stage 2; that remains an operating hypothesis. With failed upstairs valve feedback, a thermostat call alone has not produced MC-1 Mix 2 demand. Therefore stage overlap alone does not prove the main loop will run during an upstairs forced-air call. The Living Room Nest’s white W (Heat 1) splits off in the gray cabinet and goes to the black relay, which switches the Living Area input on ZCM-1. Brown */OB (configured as Heat 2) goes to MABS EZ-4 Zone 1 W. The Living Room Heat 1 conductor bypasses MABS. The MABS equipment cable to AHU-1 is suspected. The homeowner traced white Nest W to relay lug 3 and transformer common to lug 1. Relay lug 2 goes by red wire to ZCM-1 Living Area THERMOSTAT terminal 2; lug 4 goes by white wire to terminal 3. The other Nest conductors land on MABS Zone 1: green G → G, yellow Y → Y, red R → R, brown */OB → W, and blue C → M1. The blue landing is confirmed by the trace; its use as the Nest common follows from the Nest C landing. A separate white damper conductor is visible at M6. title: 01 — System architecture and equipment
text: 01 — System architecture and equipment The homeowner reports that the system was first installed when the house was built in 1999 . The current Grundfos main-loop circulator carries production code PC 1240 (week 40 of 2012), identifying it as a later replacement. Its installation date is unknown. Heat source and hydraulics [USER] Two Polaris gas water heaters in series provide hot water for hydronic radiant heat and hydronic air-handler heating. Domestic hot water and space heating share the same water, per the homeowner. The right Polaris tank in the entrance photo supplies domestic hot water through a separate Caleffi thermostatic mixing valve above the tank. The homeowner reports a tank setting around 170 °F and a mixed domestic outlet around 105–110 °F. The homeowner confirmed from the SupplyHouse receipt that TMV-2 is a Caleffi 521 MixCal, SKU 521519AC, a 3/4-inch sweat three-way thermostatic mixing valve with temperature gauge and check valve. See the overhead mixer photo . [USER TRACE] The street cold-water branch feeds both the cold inlet of the domestic Caleffi mixer (TMV-2) and the left Polaris tank, at its lower side port labeled Cold Inlet. Left and right refer to the entrance view. [USER TRACE] Domestic hot water has a passive gravity recirculation loop. Both its supply and return connect to the right Polaris tank as seen from the entrance. The homeowner reports that it keeps hot water available in much of the house. The return descends between the tanks in the entrance photo, wraps around the right tank to its far side, and enters its lower side port labeled Cold Inlet. Copper from the top hot outlet of the right tank feeds the TMV-2 hot inlet. Street cold water enters the opposite port. The mixed outlet opposite the adjustment handle starts the domestic recirculation loop. [DOC] Homeowner water-heater note identifies model PG10 34-150-2NV , confirmed on both tank nameplates. Notes include condensate trap 186642-000 , O-ring AS568-327, 1.725-inch ID , stainless washer 2.187-inch diameter × .030-inch . These are parts research notes, not confirmed installed parts. [USER] Basement radiant is independent of DuoMix, with a dedicated on/off Taco 006-B4-11 circulator switched by a Honeywell R8222D1014 relay and Caleffi 521 thermostatic mixing valve. [USER/PHOTO] Two radiant mixed-temperature groups are controlled by a Wirsbo DuoMix 201 with separate Mix 1 and Mix 2 circulation outputs and Var 1/Var 2 injection pump outputs. [USER] Upstairs circulator Taco 008-BC6 ; researched replacement cartridge 008-045RP (compatibility still verify against nameplate). The homeowner identifies this pump as the Mix 2 mixed-water circulator. [USER] Two Lennox AM30 hydronic air handlers, one basement and one attic, provide supplemental forced air. The internal circulator nameplates for both AHU-1 and AHU-2 read Taco 006-B4-11 . Product-family PDF bundled; the basement AHU-1 cabinet is AM30Q2/3-70-2, serial 5898M07675. The attic AHU-2 cabinet is AM30Q2-40-2, serial 5801K48409. Detailed field wiring remains unverified. Controls cabinet [PHOTO] Two three-zone Wirsbo circuit boards on right side, one above the other; five visible external black relays: two above ZCM-1 and three above ZCM-2, mounted above respective boards; Wirsbo DuoMix 201 and other control board on left; dense multiconductor wiring. [USER] Trol-A-Temp MABS EZ-4 four-zone panel confirmed on cover. Zone assignments are mapped. Installed staging remains unverified. [PHOTO] Original proposed radiant piping drawing photographed; Garage Entry was proposed but [USER] not installed . Known versus inferred relationships [USER] Mix 1 corresponds to first-floor radiant; Mix 2 corresponds to upstairs radiant. [INFERENCE] A zone call must ultimately be converted to DuoMix demand and a switched circulator output; exact intervening components unknown. [OPEN] All valve locations, hydronic manifold layout, piping check valves, pump positions, sensor placement, boiler enable wiring, and safety interlocks. Equipment behind the Polaris tanks [USER/PHOTO] Basement radiant uses the lower-left Taco circulator and adjacent mechanical Caleffi mixing valve. [USER/PHOTO] The red Grundfos UPS 26-99 BFC (product 52722518) runs the main circulation loop upstairs and back. It corresponds to the pump shown above the tanks on the proposed drawing. Flow is left to right in the behind-tank photo. The homeowner reports that the loop rises to the attic AM30 (AHU-2) first, then continues to the Var 2 injection and Mix 2 radiant assembly, where the piping branches. MC-1 Boiler Enable switches pump hot from terminal 6 to terminal 5. A basement-only radiant call runs its own Taco. The basement-only call does not send a demand to MC-1, so that call does not start the Grundfos. [USER/PHOTO] The two higher light-brown Taco pumps are MC-1 Mix 1 on the left and Var 1 on the right, viewed from behind the tanks. [USER/PHOTO] The first-floor Honeywell valves run front to back in this view in the order Master Bath, Master Bedroom, then Main (Living Area). Two expansion tanks are visible below and to the right. Their circuit connections remain to be traced. [USER TRACE] At the right edge of the behind-tank basement photo, the near riser is the attic supply from the red Grundfos. The return riser is partly obscured directly behind it. It drops vertically, crosses the basement plumbing at the two expansion-tank connections, then continues to the Polaris return. The second-floor heating return enters the left Polaris tank at the port labeled “Heating System Inlet.” The heating circuit passes through the left tank first and then the right tank. See the behind-tank photo . Attic hydronic piping [USER/PHOTO] In the right-hand plumbing-wall view, the lowest horizontal run is the incoming main-loop supply from the basement. The AM30 coil branch comes off first and projects toward the camera. The main loop continues toward the Var 2 injection and Mix 2 radiant assembly, then returns downstairs. [USER/PHOTO] The brown Taco on the radiant supply is Mix 2. The Taco above the red and green valve handles on the right is Var 2. Mix 2 is a Taco 008-BC6 and flows right to left in this view. Var 2 flows upward. Its Taco nameplate appears to read 008-BC6 , pending confirmation because of glare. [USER/PHOTO] In the attic plumbing-wall photo, the Rest of Second Floor supply continues left through the left valve. The Yellow Room supply turns back to the right before passing through the right valve. The uppermost cross-frame pipe is the Rest of Second Floor manifold return, which tees into the Yellow Room return. The closely spaced supply and return elbows are separate pipes. [USER TRACE] Along the attic mixed-loop return toward the Mix 2 inlet, the Yellow Room and Rest of Second Floor manifold returns combine first. The connection back to the main branch is next, followed by the Var 2 discharge tee, then the Mix 2 inlet. Var 2 draws from the main supply from the basement downstream of the AHU-2 branch and injects upward into the pipe feeding Mix 2. [USER TRACE] Along the attic main loop from the basement, the AHU-2 coil supply tee comes first and the coil outlet rejoins the main a few inches downstream. Farther along the main loop, the Var 2 inlet and the Mix 2 circuit return connect through a second pair of closely spaced tees. [USER TRACE] In the attic plumbing-wall photo with the Honeywell MiniZone panel, the main-loop return is on the left and the supply is on the right. Both pass vertically through the framed wall’s bottom plate below the visible area. [USER/PHOTO] SUP 2 is located under the insulation immediately upstream of the Mix 2 inlet. The visible blue leads carry a tekmar 071 tag. See the sensor close-up . [USER/PHOTO] The high-point air eliminator beside the visible Honeywell valve is in service. The switch labeled “Furnace” powers AHU-2, a Lennox AM30 hydronic air handler. See the right-hand attic photo . The Yellow Room radiant manifold is at the far end of the attic mechanical room beside Var 2. In the manifold photo, the right header with the small valves supplies the floor loops and the left header collects their return. The Rest of Second Floor radiant manifold has its supply on the lower, farther header with the small valves. The upper, nearer header collects the return. Polaris heating supply branches [USER TRACE] The upper side port labeled Heating System Outlet on the right Polaris tank (entrance view) feeds the heating supply header. In order from the tank, the first tee feeds the basement radiant loop, the second tee feeds the red Grundfos, and the elbow beyond both tees feeds the basement Lennox AM30 (AHU-1). The basement radiant branch has its own Taco circulator and Caleffi mixer. See the outlet branch photo . [USER TRACE] The basement radiant manifold return comes around the corner toward the expansion tanks, rises, and tees into the common heating return just beyond the expansion-tank connections, toward the left Polaris Heating System Inlet. The nearby tees serve separate connections. Their spacing does not indicate a paired supply and return connection for the basement radiant circuit. [USER/PHOTO] A temperature probe is mounted on the common heating return downstream of the basement radiant return tee, left of the expansion tanks. Its blue leads are visible behind the Grundfos. See the return probe photo . [USER TRACE] The basement AM30 (AHU-1) coil return joins the same common heating return near the left Polaris Heating System Inlet. The green-handled valve in the heating outlet branch photo identifies the AM30 return line. [USER TRACE] The insulated intertank pipe runs from the left Polaris upper Heating System Outlet to the right Polaris lower Heating System Inlet . Left and right refer to the entrance view. The second-floor heating return enters the left tank, passes through both tanks in series, and leaves the right tank through its Heating System Outlet. See the intertank pipe photo . First-floor radiant injection piping [USER TRACE] Var 1 (right pump, Taco 008-BC6 ) draws from the main loop as it returns from upstairs. That branch feeds the Mix 1 circuit, which rejoins the same main return through the other of two closely spaced tees at the right of the photo. Mix 1 is the left pump, a Taco 006-B4-11 . Both pumps flow right to left in this view. The blue sensor lead is visible immediately upstream of Mix 1. The blue sensor leads splice to red and white conductors in a brown-jacketed thermostat cable. A red conductor lands on MC-1 SUP 1, making this the inferred SUP 1 sensor. The cable disappears into a bundle before the controller, so end-to-end identity and the white conductor termination remain unverified. See the Mix 1 and Var 1 close-up . [USER TRACE] Mix 1 discharge splits into three branches for Master Bath, Master Bedroom, and Main (Living Area). Each branch passes through its Honeywell zone valve before reaching its supply manifold. Elbows turn the flow left to right through the valves toward the manifolds in the overhead view. See the overhead photo . [USER TRACE] The Master Bath, Master Bedroom, and Main (Living Area) returns collect in one common first-floor return manifold visible just below Mix 1 in the Mix 1 and Var 1 close-up. From that manifold toward Mix 1, the lower pipe below Var 1 connects back to the main return first. Farther along, Var 1 discharges into the pipe feeding the Mix 1 inlet. Var 1 draws from the main loop returning from upstairs. Basement radiant mixer and manifold [USER/PHOTO] The hot supply from the right Polaris heating header enters the Caleffi mixer from above. The basement Taco circulator is in the foreground and the manifold is behind it. At the right behind the wiring, the front and rear pipes visually overlap and remain separate at that point. The Caleffi mixed outlet runs left through the branch with the red-handled valve to the Taco inlet. The bottom port runs down and across to the basement radiant return manifold. The manifold return continues downstream to its tee into the common heating return by the expansion tanks. The Taco discharge feeds the basement radiant supply manifold directly. See the basement radiant close-up . Basement pressure instrumentation The combination temperature and pressure gauge is mounted on the Mix 1 discharge, between the circulator and the three main-floor Honeywell zone valves. The October 1, 1999 Lennox CompleteHeat dealer letter describes an external pressure-reducing valve and expansion tank requirement. The homeowner traced the street cold-water feed to the Polaris and domestic mixer branch and saw no identifiable pressure-reducing valve along the route. Presence elsewhere remains unverified. See the letter and gauge photos .

title: 04 — Wiring discoveries, cable sharing, valve logic
text: 04 — Wiring discoveries, cable sharing, valve logic Brown-sheathed multiconductor cables [USER] Several 6- or 8-conductor thermostat-style cables leave the top of cabinet. Within a single sheath, conductors are split across multiple purposes; cable co-location does not prove electrical association. [USER] Bedroom Above Garage / Yellow Room: brown and blue conductors go to DuoMix 17 COM / 20 SUP 2 . A small temperature sensor contacts the supply pipe at the far end. The installer apparently reused spare thermostat-cable conductors for this sensor; whether it is physically part of the thermostat cable and exact route should be documented. [USER] Rest of Second Floor: brown conductors from its cable go to the black external relays; user noted wires appearing to reach two different relays . Which terminal and which relay is not yet established. [PHOTO] Relay wiring connects to upper THERMOSTAT terminals of ZCM-2 radiant zone control module. This suggests a possible input/isolation role, but direction of electrical signal remains unknown. [PHOTO] ZCM-2 right-edge OUTPUT strip has visible red conductors; exact number/terminal locations and destination not traced. Competing topology hypotheses A. Thermostat → external relay coil → relay contact → Wirsbo THERMOSTAT input → board OUTPUT → DuoMix Mix 2 Demand. B. Thermostat → Wirsbo THERMOSTAT input; TELESTAT or OUTPUT energizes relay/zone valve; Honeywell end switch triggers DuoMix demand. C. Thermostat staging relay independently distributes stage-1 and stage-2 calls to Wirsbo and Lennox controls. None is proven. Avoid diagramming any as verified. Honeywell zone valves [PHOTO] Yellow Room valve is a Honeywell V8043E1061 , normally closed. The two yellow leads power its 24 VAC motor. The two red leads are the separate auxiliary end switch. Confirm nameplates individually on the other valves. [DOC] A motor-driven call should close the auxiliary switch at the end of the opening stroke. The manual-open lever does not operate it. The isolated pair should read OL closed-valve, near 0 ohms fully open on a call, then OL after closing. Honeywell instructions [USER] Yellow Room red leads splice to green and yellow in a brown thermostat cable. A matching pair lands at its ZCM-2 lower TELESTAT R1/R2. End-to-end cable identity and exact color-to-terminal assignment remain unverified. Motor routing and other zone wiring remain open. Both upstairs switches stayed OL when tested at the valves during motor-driven calls. See test log . title: 05 — Active fault: second-floor radiant circulator

It cannot establish end-switch closure or determine whether the ZCM is faulty. Both upstairs inputs dropped to 0 VAC on a call even though their isolated valve end switches read OL. Verify closure independently, then assess the module by its ES output and the corresponding DuoMix demand response with verified feedback applied. Current diagnosis: Both upstairs valves moved on a call but their isolated end switches stayed OL. The working Living Room switch showed continuity during demand. Inspect valve travel and switch actuation first. ZCM-2 replacement is deferred until its response to valid feedback can be checked. Symptom [USER] Rest of Second Floor thermostat calls for heat; the corresponding ZCM-2 radiant zone control module yellow indicator illuminates, but DuoMix LCD shows no visible response and Mix 2 mixed-water circulator does not receive 120 V at DuoMix terminal 8 under test conditions. By contrast, a first-floor call produces 120 V at Mix 1 mixed-water circulator terminal 12 . Do not extrapolate voltage readings to other conditions; the meter reference, time since call, and settings were not logged. What is actually established Thermostat call correlates with lower radiant zone control module zone-1 yellow indicator. At least some electrical path reaches or affects the radiant zone control module; LED meaning not independently verified. Mix 2 mixed-water circulator switched-hot output was not active when checked; this does not by itself prove DuoMix fault. Mix 1 output is capable of energizing during a different zone call. No visible LCD change was reported; display interpretation remains unverified. The Yellow Room's 17/20 conductors are supply sensor, not Mix 2 demand . Fault tree (unverified branches) Missing demand at DuoMix 3–4: board OUTPUT issue, upstream external relay/contact, Honeywell valve end switch (if used), loose wire, staging control. Demand reaches DuoMix but output inhibited: control logic, sensor/outdoor conditions, settings, pump protection, internal relay failure. Apparent failure due to test conditions: time delay, sensor state, incomplete thermostat call, wrong meter reference, wrong assumed output. Test plan (visual/non-invasive first) Photograph DuoMix 3–4 and follow each conductor physically to source. Record cable IDs and terminal labels. Photograph external relay part numbers and all terminals; trace contacts versus coils with power safely isolated and qualified assistance. Identify Honeywell valve model and observe mechanical position during sustained call; trace any end-switch wires. Document the right-side OUTPUT labels and wires on ZCM-2 (installed part A303XX0003 ). Locate manufacturer's instructions before electrical testing. Record all indicators and DuoMix display during controlled, sustained upstairs demand; note elapsed minutes and room/pipe temperatures. If professionally tested, compare actual state of DuoMix 3–4 with active call to determine upstream versus controller-side fault; never short terminals or inject voltage without confirmed manufacturer instructions. Prior service clue [USER] Replacement Wirsbo zone-controller box contained handwritten note “no output on zone 3.” Board/date/author and meaning of output unknown. Current problem is lower radiant zone control module zone 1 , so the note is context, not diagnosis. Whether a removed board is in box was asked but not answered. 2026-11-07: simultaneous upstairs zone demand (new photographs) [USER] Both upstairs zones (Rest of Second Floor and Bedroom Above Garage) calling at once. [OBSERVED PHOTO] DuoMix 201 LCD reads OPEN with upper item text not confidently transcribed. User reports neither upstairs call appears as a Mix 2 demand on DuoMix. This does not prove whether terminals 3–4 are open, or what OPEN refers to; it may be a selected diagnostic/menu value rather than a global demand status. Do not assume amber LEDs prove valve position or contact closure. In the traced demand circuit, that is consistent with an open or high-resistance ES path. The reading alone cannot distinguish a relay that was never commanded from a failed contact or a wiring fault, or establish what MC-1 sees across terminals 3 and 4. Unverified causes: Missing actuator travel or end-switch feedback, an external interlock or wiring fault, or a fault in the ZCM-2 ES relay or associated circuitry. The installed A303XX0003 activation sequence remains unverified. Traced wiring: Upper ES brown -> DuoMix 1; lower ES upper red -> DuoMix 3; lower ES lower white -> upper radiant zone control module -> apparent 24 VAC transformer; DuoMix 2 and 4 tied together. ES terminals are not the separate OUTPUT terminals. [USER] Yellow Room call: The initial closed-valve observation was made after the call had stopped. On a renewed call, the homeowner heard the valve operate and saw it move toward open. This supports actuator drive reaching the valve. On recheck during the same call, yellow remained lit, lower red stayed off, and the valve still felt open. [USER] Yellow Room repeat cycle: With the zone satisfied, lower TELESTAT R1/R2 measured 10.69 VAC. During the renewed call, yellow lit and voltage held near 10.3 VAC before dropping to 0 VAC, confirmed at both the exposed conductors and the screws. Red stayed off. This matches the delayed drop and dark red LED seen on Rest of Second Floor. The satisfied reading differs from the earlier 0 VAC observation. During this call, ZCM-2 ES measured about 27 VAC. End-switch closure has not been independently verified. [USER] Yellow Room isolated valve end-switch test: Honeywell V8043E1061 red leads disconnected from the green/yellow feedback cable at the valve. On a renewed call, the valve visibly reopened, with 0.11 VAC and OL across the isolated red leads. After satisfying the call, the pair read 0 VAC and OL. No end-switch closure was observed directly at the valve. Full travel and switch actuation remain unverified. See the separate Rest of Second Floor isolated test below. [USER] Rest of Second Floor isolated valve end-switch test: At the valve, the isolated end-switch pair measured 0 VAC and OL while satisfied. On a renewed call the valve appeared fully open, but the pair still measured 0 VAC and OL. After satisfying the call, the homeowner felt the valve close and reported 0 VAC throughout. Neither upstairs valve produced a measured end-switch closure at the valve. Check end-switch actuation or travel before ordering ZCM-2. This verifies that the test setup detects closure on a working zone. Both upstairs valves remained OL after opening, making valve-side end-switch actuation or travel the priority. ZCM-2 operation with valid feedback remains unverified. Defer board replacement pending valve-side diagnosis. [USER] Additional ZCM-1 comparison: Master Bath calling with valve open and about 0 VAC at TELESTAT R1/R2. Master Bedroom was satisfied while its switch also appeared closed. The exact contact referred to as the M switch and the method used to establish closure remain unverified. Yellow Room was satisfied and its valve was closed. Next observation: During a sustained upstairs call, record whether the red indicator stays off, flashes, or goes solid and whether the corresponding actuator opens. Compare with ZCM-1. Identify the actuator model and trace any feedback wiring. Verify the installed board’s indicator meanings before using them to distinguish missing feedback from a fault in the ES switching path. Replacement: Uponor A3031003 remains an unverified candidate. Before ordering, confirm compatibility with the installed thermostats, actuators, ES demand circuit, ZCM-1 interconnection and mounting. Meter correction: Earlier assistant misread multimeter photograph as DC; homeowner confirmed the original 27.2 V readings were taken with the AC squiggle selected. Active issue B — Upstairs/attic Lennox AM30 air-handler pump [USER, 2026-11-07] Homeowner reports a bad pump on the upstairs (attic) Lennox AM30 hydronic air handler . This is a separate active issue from the Mix 2 mixed-water circulator fault. [UNKNOWN] Symptoms, failure mode, whether seized/failed electrically, supply voltage, control demand, isolation valves, and whether it is hydronic coil circulation or another function. [DO NOT CONFLATE] The upstairs AM30 air-handler hydronic circulator is not assumed to be DuoMix Mix 2 Pmp (terminal 8), Var 2 Pmp (terminal 10), or Taco 008-BC6 until physically traced. [NEXT] Record the full AM30 cabinet model and serial number, document precise symptoms, determine which thermostat stage calls it, trace its supply/control, and identify safe service/replacement options. AHU-2 cartridge identification and availability [PHOTO] Homeowner photo 55573.jpg identifies the upstairs AM30 circulator as Taco 006-B4-11 , rated 115 V, 60 Hz, 1/40 hp. Pump failure and its cause remain unverified. [TACO] The exact 006-B4-11 row specifies cartridge assembly 006-040RP and casing O-ring 007-003RP . Current stock and an approved supersession were not verified. SupplyHouse explicitly excludes the 006-B4-11 from its 005-020RP fitment list. Taco parts list · SupplyHouse listing [LENNOX] Table 6 lists the original-equipment cartridge kits by air-handler model. AM30-40 and AM30-70 use 99K70 (99K7001) . AM30-90, AM30-105 and AM30-120 use 73J77 (73J7701) . The photographed attic cabinet AM30Q2-40-2 falls in the AM30-40 group, making 99K70 the Lennox catalog match. A direct manufacturer cross-reference from 006-040RP to either kit has not been verified. Lennox service manual · LennoxPros catalog [SOURCING] Parts Town lists 99K70 , with live stock unconfirmed. Use the confirmed attic cabinet model AM30Q2-40-2 and serial 5801K48409 plus the pump nameplate to check kit fit, stock and any supersession with a Lennox dealer. Parts Town listing Open question: upstairs forced-air heat and main-loop flow The upstairs radiant fault may prevent the main loop from supplying hot water to the attic AHU during a supplemental heat call, if the air circuit relies on an overlapping radiant call. The Living Room trace does not establish upstairs staging, overlap, or pump power. Missing main-loop flow could explain a cold coil even with the internal pump running; it does not establish why the pump would be unpowered or stationary. Restore upstairs radiant demand, then check main-loop flow, AHU heat demand, and internal pump operation separately before concluding the pump failed.

title: 07 — Reconstructed conversation history, corrections and reasoning
text: 07 — Reconstructed conversation history, corrections and reasoning This is a detailed topical reconstruction, not a word-for-word transcript. Exact full previous-chat text was not provided as an export. Some earlier photos may have been discussed before the currently mounted set; all locally mounted original images are included. System discovery. User established two Polaris heaters in series, six installed radiant zones, five air thermostats, two AM30 hydronic air handlers, separate basement Caleffi mixing, and DuoMix dual mixed circuits. Original piping diagram is proposed and includes uninstalled Garage Entry. Control identification. DuoMix 201 part A3030005 / March 1999; earlier research about proMix 201 and tekmar 374 was recognized as potentially conflated. Board terminal functions and LCD labels were photographed. Symptom isolated. First-floor call produces 120 V at DuoMix terminal 12, while upstairs call does not energize terminal 8. DuoMix LCD appears unchanged on upstairs call. Wirsbo lower radiant zone control module inspection. Zone 1 yellow indicator responds to Rest of Second Floor thermostat. Top terminal strips labeled THERMOSTAT; bottom TELESTAT; right side OUTPUT. LED semantics were initially over-interpreted; currently unverified . Historic replacement box. Handwritten note 'no output on zone 3' found inside a replacement radiant zone control module box. Which board, date, channel and type of output unclear. User did not yet confirm whether an old board is in the box. Distinct OUTPUT strip. User recognized the right-side OUTPUT is separate from THERMOSTAT and TELESTAT. This suggests a possible demand interface to DuoMix, but no physical trace established . MABS question. User asked whether MABS or Wirsbo receives thermostat signal first. Assistant hypothesized MABS first, explicitly not verified ; alternative direct-to-Wirsbo exists. Telestat definition. Assistant explained Wirsbo thermal actuator mechanism, but user corrected: actual installed zone valves are Honeywell motorized valves . Thus generic Wirsbo thermal actuator photos and opening delays must not be assumed to describe installed valves. Black relay photo. User showed three black modules above ZCM-2 radiant zone control module, another three above upper. Wires lead to Wirsbo THERMOSTAT terminals. Hypotheses: isolation/staging relays, valve control, contact logic; not yet identified. Multiconductor cable tracing. User found brown-sheathed cables leaving cabinet. Yellow Room's brown/blue conductors connect to DuoMix 17 COM and 20 SUP 2; a pipe-mounted sensor is present, so these are supply-temperature sensing, not zone demand. Rest of Second Floor cable's brown wires route to external black relays (possibly two different relays). Other conductors in sheath serve thermostat functions. Cable co-location is not evidence of common purpose. Supply sensor versus VAR2. Sensor informs variable injection pump modulation/temperature regulation; Mix 2 Demand at 3–4 is distinct and remains key unknown. Master document. A v0.1 DOCX and PDF were generated with 11 sections, zone table, terminal map, hypotheses, 18 initial open questions. Both archived in this ZIP. The present Markdown knowledge base expands that transfer with source files and all available photos. Current request. User wants all available photos and comprehensive Markdown reference/index in a ZIP to bring into ChatGPT Work. This bundle is that portable handoff. Claims explicitly withdrawn or downgraded 'MABS definitely comes before Wirsbo' → unproven. 'Yellow LED proves thermostat demand output' → LED may instead indicate TELESTAT/output; manual needed. 'Telestat actuators are installed' → false; Honeywell valves installed. 'Black relays open zone valves' → plausible, not proven. 'Right-side OUTPUT directly feeds DuoMix 3–4' → plausible, not traced. 'DuoMix 201 is tekmar 374' → unverified model cross-reference. 'Supply 2 temperature sensor initiates Mix 2 mixed-water circulator' → incomplete; sensor modulates temperature control, distinct from heat demand. 'Historic zone 3 fault explains present zone 1 problem' → no evidence of direct causal link. 2026-11-07 — ES wiring, multimeter and comparative diagnostic readings Homeowner confirmed demand wiring: ZCM-1 ES brown -> DuoMix 1; lower ES red -> DuoMix 3; lower ES white -> upper radiant zone control module -> apparent transformer; DuoMix 2/4 tied. The distinct OUTPUT terminals were differentiated from ES. The multimeter was correctly in V~ AC mode; an earlier assistant misreading was corrected. Upper ES read 27.2 VAC with no first-floor call, ~1 VAC with call; lower ES read 27.2 VAC with both upstairs zones calling and both satisfied. Leading fault hypothesis: lower ES contacts not closing or a required condition for closure not being met. Root cause unconfirmed. Upstairs valve feedback and working comparison The Yellow Room valve nameplate confirmed Honeywell V8043E1061. Its red switch leads splice to a green/yellow pair with matching colors at ZCM-2 TELESTAT R1/R2. Both upstairs valves opened on a call, but their isolated end switches stayed OL. The working Living Room switch changed from OL to continuity. Connected R1/R2 voltage fell to 0 VAC on both upstairs calls despite the open switches. Defer ZCM-2 replacement until valve feedback is restored and its ES response can be tested. The separate attic AM30 circulator was identified as Taco 006-B4-11. See the field tests and cartridge research .

The Lennox dealer/installer letter dated October 1, 1999 describes a CompleteHeat installation requirement for an external 3/4-inch water pressure-reducing valve and thermal expansion tank. It cites unregulated supply pressure above 55 psi and large fluctuations as concerns. This is historical product documentation. The presence and location of a pressure-reducing valve in the current Polaris piping remain unverified. The basement instrument is a combination temperature and pressure gauge. The photo shows approximately 90 °F and 65 psi on the inner blue pressure scale. The homeowner identifies its location as the Mix 1 discharge before the three main-floor zone valves. Operating conditions and gauge accuracy remain unverified. Basement AM30 cabinet nameplate Lennox AM30Q2/3-70-2 , serial 5898M07675 . The plate lists 120 V, 60 Hz, single phase, a 1/40 hp water pump rated 0.52 A, and a maximum water inlet temperature of 180 °F. It specifies potable-water-compatible piping and fittings and prohibits adding boiler treatment chemicals. Basement AM30 wiring diagram The cabinet door carries the Lennox AM30-2 Series factory wiring diagram, form 532,890W , dated 6/98 . It shows the thermostat terminal block, blower speed taps, water-pump circuits, freeze-stat, and HM30 interface. Field wiring and optional components require separate verification. Basement AM30 circulator nameplate The internal AHU-1 circulator is a Taco 006-B4-11 , rated 115 V, 60 Hz, 0.52 A and 1/40 hp. The attic AHU-2 has a separate pump of the same model. Attic AM30 and circulator nameplates AHU-2 is Lennox AM30Q2-40-2 , serial 5801K48409 . The cabinet plate lists a maximum water inlet temperature of 180 °F. The internal circulator is Taco 006-B4-11 , rated 115 V, 60 Hz, 0.52 A and 1/40 hp. Basement radiant circulator nameplate The dedicated basement radiant circulator is a Taco 006-B4-11 , rated 115 V, 60 Hz, 0.52 A and 1/40 hp. Both AM30 internal circulators also use this model. Mix 1 circulator nameplate Mix 1 is a Taco 006-B4-11 , rated 115 V, 60 Hz, 0.52 A and 1/40 hp. The nameplate faces the wall and a manifold hose partly blocks it, making it unreadable from the usual service position. This close-up captures the identifying details. Var 1 circulator nameplate Var 1 is a Taco 008-BC6 , rated 115 V, 60 Hz, 0.84 A and 1/25 hp. DuoMix 201 terminal strip Straight-on view of MC-1 showing the demand, line-voltage and sensor terminals. The sensor strip spans terminals 17–27. A blue lead is visible at 20 Sup2 and a red lead at 23 Sup1 . The faceplate marks the sensor strip “Do not apply power.” See the terminal reference . Common heating return temperature probe The blue leads behind the Grundfos enter insulation on the common heating return. The probe is left of the expansion tanks and downstream of the basement radiant return tee, toward the left Polaris. It is the likely MC-1 BRet sensor. The cable termination has yet to be traced. Basement MABS EZ-4 panel The Trol-A-Temp MABS EZ-4 is mounted below the DuoMix. The cover diagram documents factory terminal functions. The installed board is labeled Living Room, Master Bedroom and Basement for Zones 1–3. See the controls reference . Basement AM30 low-voltage wiring The close-up shows the five-screw TB1 block and multiple field conductors. The wider view places it at the bottom of the control board, below the pump wiring. See the factory diagram and field observations . Duct dampers reference photo The photo shows damper actuators on duct branches. Retained for reference. The current survey covers plumbing and main system controls through the Lennox AM30 units. ZCM boards, relays and zone tags This cabinet view shows two black relay assemblies above ZCM-1 and three between the boards, above ZCM-2. Visible cable tags include Living Area, Master Bedroom, Master Bath, and Bedroom Above Garage. ZCM-1 is marked A303XX0003. The relay model and pinout are unreadable from this angle. Upper ZCM relay nameplates Above ZCM-1, the right relay is MARS 90293 (label also shows D4600), and the left relay is White-Rodgers 90-293Q . Both labels specify a 24 VAC, 50/60 Hz coil. The nearby zone tags label cables. Relay assignments require a wiring trace. Lower-right relay above ZCM-2 The side label shows White-Rodgers, a 24 V 50/60 Hz coil, and a printed switching diagram. Wiring obscures the exact model number. The nearby SPARE tag identifies a cable. Its relationship to this relay remains unverified. Cabinet Honeywell switching relay Front view of the brown Honeywell R8222D1014 beside MC-1. Its 24 VAC coil shares a transformer conductor with the two upper black relays. The switched black lead feeds the basement radiant Taco. Living Room thermostat cable split Cabinet photo showing the white Heat 1 wire splitting off to the relay . Wiring trace and terminal assignments .

title: 08 — Photo catalog › Mechanical room overview
text: View from the entrance. Both Polaris tanks are centered, the basement Lennox AM30 (AHU-1) is on the left, and the controls cabinet is on the right. The downstairs circulators are behind the tanks and out of view. Use this image to orient the plumbing survey. Supply and return paths still need to be traced. The homeowner identifies the Caleffi mixer above the right Polaris tank as the domestic hot-water tempering valve. The domestic and space-heating circuits share the same water. The passive domestic recirculation return drops between the tanks, wraps around the right tank, and enters its lower Cold Inlet on the far side. The equivalent port on the left tank receives street cold water. The mixer receives hot water from the top of the right tank and street cold water at the opposite port. The mixed outlet opposite the adjustment handle starts the domestic recirculation loop.

title: 08 — Photo catalog › Behind the Polaris tanks
text: The homeowner identifies the lower-left Taco as the basement radiant circulator and the adjacent Caleffi as its mechanical mixing valve. The red Grundfos above and to the right circulates the main loop upstairs and back. It corresponds to the pump drawn above the Polaris tanks on the original proposed piping diagram. Of the two light-brown Taco pumps higher in the photo, MC-1 Mix 1 is on the left and Var 1 is on the right. Both pumps flow right to left in this view. Three first-floor Honeywell zone valves sit in a row, front to back in this view. Their order is Master Bath, Master Bedroom, then Main (Living Area). The nearest valve, labeled Master Bath, is visible. Two expansion tanks are visible at lower right. The red Grundfos flows left to right in this view. The loop goes to the attic AM30 first, then to the Var 2 and Mix 2 assembly. At the right edge, the nearer riser is the supply from the Grundfos. Behind it, the partly obscured return drops vertically, crosses past the two expansion-tank connections, and continues to the Polaris return.

title: 08 — Photo catalog › Attic mechanical room overview
text: The attic Lennox AM30 (AHU-2) is on the right and the hydronic piping is on the left. The homeowner identifies the black foam-insulated pipes crossing toward the unit as the AM30 coil piping. The unit houses the Taco 006-B4-11 circulator under separate investigation. Supply and return identification in this view is pending.

title: 08 — Photo catalog › Attic plumbing wall
text: The two upstairs Honeywell motorized valves are visible high on the wall above the Honeywell MiniZone panel. The homeowner identifies these as the valves tested for the Yellow Room and Rest of Second Floor. The left valve serves Rest of Second Floor and the right valve serves Yellow Room. The Rest of Second Floor supply continues left through its valve. The Yellow Room supply turns back to the right before reaching its valve. The homeowner suspects a direct connection between the wall thermostat and MiniZone. The panel model, terminal assignments and cable routing remain to be verified. In this view, the main-loop return is on the left and the main-loop supply is on the right. The homeowner traced both pipes straight down through the framed wall’s bottom plate, below the visible area.

The homeowner reports that the high-point air eliminator beside the valve is in service. The brown Taco on the radiant supply is Mix 2. The Taco on the right above the red and green valve handles is Var 2. The pipes projecting toward the camera serve the AM30 coil. See the attic pipe routing .

title: 10 — Work session handoff and update workflow
text: 10 — Work session handoff and update workflow Suggested initial instruction for ChatGPT Work Unpack this ZIP, read README.md, INDEX.md and all Markdown notes, inspect every photo in photos/, and treat this as the current Englewood Rd. heating system knowledge base. Distinguish observed facts from hypotheses. Do not assume an as-built circuit unless traced. Help identify the ZCM-2 OUTPUT circuit, the external black relay models, Honeywell valve wiring and DuoMix Mix 2 Demand 3–4 path. Maintain the Markdown files and image catalog as discoveries are made, and package a new version for export when requested. Work priorities Resolve Mix 2 demand wiring with original photographs and new close-ups. Identify external relay pinout and Honeywell valve/end-switch wiring. Find correct DuoMix 201 A3030005 manual and zone-board documentation, not similarly named proMix. Develop verified as-built schematic and cable schedule. Update the master reference with confidence tags and test log. Template for each field observation ### YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM — observation title - Zone / thermostat / setpoint: - Equipment, terminal IDs and wire colors: - What was directly seen: - Meter reading (if any): meter points, AC/DC, value, elapsed time: - Photo filename: - Interpretation [INFERENCE]: - Alternative explanation: - Follow-up: Files and portability Keep relative links stable. Never overwrite original photos; add annotated derivatives separately. Update MANIFEST.tsv when assets change. This bundle is portable but does not automatically migrate the original ChatGPT conversation's exact messages or private Project state into Work. As-built capture plan Survey scope covers plumbing and main system controls through the Lennox AM30 units. Downstream ductwork and damper tracing are deferred. Start with two overlapping wide photos of the mechanical room from opposite angles. Include the Polaris tanks and nearby pipe branches. Trace supply and return by branch. Cover basement radiant, Mix 1, Mix 2, and both AM30s. Photograph pump nameplates, flow arrows, mixing valves, and points where pipes disappear. Map pump and valve cables to their boards and terminals. Distinguish the Mix 2 circulator, Var 2 injection pump, Taco 008-BC6, and attic AM30 Taco 006-B4-11. Observe a working radiant call and a forced-air call. Record thermostat, valve, ZCM, DuoMix, relay and pump changes. Keep unresolved MABS and staging links visible. Use the same equipment labels on the plumbing map, controls map and zone table. Mark each link observed, traced or unresolved. Use the proposed piping drawing for orientation and field observations for the as-built map.

title: 11 — Report brief: executive summary and active investigations
text: 11 — Report brief: executive summary and active investigations This file provides short, source-controlled Markdown summaries for the generated HTML report. Detailed evidence remains in the topic notes. Update these sections whenever the diagnosis changes. Issue 01 — Mix 2 mixed-water circulator does not run Status: Both upstairs valve end switches stayed open during isolated tests on calls. The working Living Room switch changed from OL to continuity. Both upstairs zones have shown illuminated TELESTAT-area indicators, but DuoMix 201 has not been observed to enable Mix 2 circulation. The ZCM-2 ES pair reads 27.2 VAC whether upstairs zones are calling or satisfied , unlike the upper working ES pair, which falls from 27.2 to ~1 VAC on a first-floor call. Current diagnosis: Missing valve end-switch feedback explains the observed lack of Mix 2 demand. Check valve travel and switch actuation. ZCM-2 response to valid feedback remains unverified. Next: Resolve valve-side feedback, then verify ZCM-2 ES and MC-1 Mix 2 demand. Defer board replacement until that check. Issue 02 — AHU-2 air-handler hydronic circulator reported bad Status: Reported by homeowner; failure mode unconfirmed. The upstairs/attic Lennox AM30 hydronic air-handler pump is reported bad. The nameplate reads Taco 006-B4-11. Taco specifies cartridge 006-040RP. Stock and supersession remain unverified. See the cartridge crosswalk . Separate equipment: Do not equate this with the DuoMix Mix 2 mixed-water circulator or Var 2 injection pump without physical tracing. Next: With cabinet AM30Q2-40-2 / serial 5801K48409 now photographed, document symptoms, verify pump operation/control, and confirm kit fit and availability.

title: 12 — Standard terminology and equipment tags
text: 12 — Standard terminology and equipment tags Evidence and confidence Confirmed means directly supported by a photo, measurement, observation, or trace. Unknown means there is too little evidence to make an assignment. Inferred is the umbrella term for a claim supported by evidence but still awaiting verification. Likely: The evidence strongly favors one explanation and no plausible alternative has been identified. The common return probe is likely connected to MC-1 terminal 25 (BRet). Its location and function fit that input, and the cable still needs an end-to-end trace. Suspected: An explanation fits some observations, and plausible alternatives remain. Use this for tentative relay, ZCM, or air zone board routes and behaviors. Apply confidence to the specific claim. A board can have a confirmed model and a suspected wiring route. Status: Approved by homeowner, 2026-11-08. This register governs the Markdown notes, diagrams, and generated HTML. Tags are documentation identifiers , not verified manufacturer designations. Preserve the exact physical terminal markings (e.g., Mix 2 Pmp , Var 2 Pmp , ES , TELESTAT ) when quoting labels. Installed staging and output routing remain to be traced. 24 VAC control transformer XFMR-1 (provisional) Supplies low-voltage controls; exact shared ES circuit topology not verified Water-heating plant / hydronic heat source WH-1, WH-2 Two Polaris water heaters in series; Left tank nameplate PG10 34-150-2NV, serial 0448117372. Right tank nameplate PG10 34-150-2NV, serial 0449124485. Tags do not assert flow order Main-loop circulator — Grundfos UPS 26-99 BFC, product 52722518. Blue tape reads “Boiler Enable From Wirsbo.” MC-1 Boiler Enable terminal 6 receives line hot and terminal 5 sends switched hot to the pump. Basement radiant circulator — Dedicated on/off Taco 006-B4-11. Feeds the basement radiant supply manifold from TMV-1. Mixed-water circulator P-M1, P-M2 (provisional) DuoMix outputs Mix 1 Pmp (12) and Mix 2 Pmp (8); Mix 2 is Taco 008-BC6. Mix 1 is Taco 006-B4-11 Variable-speed injection circulator P-I1, P-I2 (provisional) DuoMix outputs Var 1 Pmp (14) and Var 2 Pmp (10); Var 1 is Taco 008-BC6. Var 2 appears to be the same model, pending nameplate confirmation Thermostatic mixing valve (TMV) TMV-1 Caleffi 521 basement radiant mixing valve Domestic hot-water tempering valve TMV-2 (provisional) Caleffi above the right Polaris tank in the entrance photo. Caleffi 521 MixCal, SupplyHouse SKU 521519AC, 3/4-inch sweat, with temperature gauge and check valve per homeowner receipt. Hydronic air-handling unit (hydronic air handler) AHU-1 Basement Lennox AM30, cabinet model AM30Q2/3-70-2, serial 5898M07675. Associated C26-41-1 refrigerant evaporator, serial 6099H46722. Hydronic air-handling unit (hydronic air handler) AHU-2 Attic Lennox AM30Q2-40-2, serial 5801K48409, with Taco 006-B4-11 circulator Air-handler hydronic circulator P-AHU1 Basement AM30 internal Taco 006-B4-11. Air-handler hydronic circulator P-AHU2 Attic AM30 internal Taco 006-B4-11. Suspected failure remains unverified. Motorized zone valve / zone-valve actuator TBD Honeywell V8043E1061 confirmed for Yellow Room. Verify other nameplates. Thermoelectric actuator / thermal actuator TBD Wirsbo TELESTAT is a terminal marking ; not evidence that this actuator type is installed System end-switch contacts ES Contact pair on each ZCM; upper pair shows demand-dependent voltage change Heating demand / call for heat — Thermostat demand condition Switched line-voltage circulator output — DuoMix pump output, e.g. terminal 8 or 12, nominal 120 VAC Mixing demand input — DuoMix terminals 1–2 and 3–4 Important distinctions: Mix 2 mixed-water circulator and the AHU-2 air-handler hydronic circulator are different suspected devices . OUTPUT and ES/ES are different terminal groups on the radiant zone control modules. MABS panel role remains provisional; no claim about thermostat sequence is justified without a trace. A3031003 is a proposed replacement candidate. Compatibility with the installed A303XX0003 modules remains unverified.

title: 13 — Current guide synthesis and scope
text: 13 — Current guide synthesis and scope Deliverable approved 2026-11-08 The primary explanatory report is now Englewood Road Hydronic Heating System , without a street number. report/index.html is one self-contained HTML file with embedded photos, interactive diagrams, searchable equipment, operating sequences, and known issues. It replaces the earlier HTML presentation. Original photographs and historical records remain preserved. The user approved conventional hydronic/electrical symbols, red/blue piping with a distinct mixed-water color, component hover previews and tap/click photo details, and a high-level-to-detail structure. The survey stops at plumbing and main electronics through both AM30 units, not downstream duct/damper mapping. Corrections that govern the current synthesis Both ZCMs are installed A303XX0003 . A3031003 remains an unverified replacement candidate; A3030003 is an earlier guessed installed identity. Both upstairs isolated valve switches remained OL during powered opening; a working Living Room comparison showed continuity. This prioritizes valve travel/switch actuation, without proving ZCM-2 healthy or defective. Connected TELESTAT R1/R2 voltage alone cannot diagnose closure or board health. Yellow Room valve is Honeywell V8043E1061. Other valve nameplates have not all been confirmed. Main heating flow: common return → left Polaris → right Polaris → branches. First tee supplies basement radiant, second supplies Grundfos, following elbow supplies basement AM30. Grundfos loop: attic AM30 closely spaced tees → upstairs injection tees → return to basement → first-floor injection tees → common return. First-floor injection draws from this returning main loop. Mixed circuits: combined manifold returns → takeoff back to main loop → injection junction → supply probe/Mix inlet. Zone branches are parallel. Two expansion tanks connect at the common return; basement radiant joins downstream toward the left tank. Nearby return tees are not automatically a primary/secondary pair. Basement radiant uses one dedicated Taco and a mechanical mixer; Honeywell R8222D1014 switches its 120 V supply. No basement radiant ZCM, MC-1 demand, or basement-only Grundfos start is reported. Shared white transformer wiring to brown and upper black relays appears to be 24 VAC common, not a demonstrated 120 V neutral. Checked ZCM upper THERMOSTAT 2 → relay lug 2 red; THERMOSTAT 3 → relay lug 4 white; SB and 4 unused. Complete relay roles remain unresolved. MC-1 Boiler Enable: terminal 6 receives 120 V hot; terminal 5 supplies Grundfos hot; pump white returns to supply neutral. It is not traced to Polaris burner enable. Domestic water is shared with heating. Street cold feeds left Polaris Cold Inlet and TMV-2 cold inlet. Right top domestic hot outlet feeds TMV-2 hot inlet; mixed outlet feeds distribution/passive recirculation; return enters right Cold Inlet. Domestic mixer is receipt-confirmed Caleffi 521519AC. Basement mixer is Caleffi 521, exact suffix unverified. Basement AM30 model AM30Q2/3-70-2, serial 5898M07675. Attic AM30Q2-40-2, serial 5801K48409. Both internal pumps are Taco 006-B4-11; so are Mix 1 and basement radiant. Mix 2 and Var 1 are 008-BC6; Var 2 appears 008-BC6, provisional due to glare. MABS EZ-4 downstairs: Zone 1 Living Area, Zone 2 Master Bedroom, Zone 3 Basement. EMM-3 attic: Zone 1 Rest of Second Floor, Zone 2 Yellow Room. Equipment-to-AM30 cable identities and staging are inferred, not traced end to end. Stage 2 retaining stage 1 is a homeowner expectation. With failed upstairs end-switch feedback, stage 1 demand alone does not prove Grundfos operation. Independent air-only main-loop enable remains open. Grundfos PC 1240 is a production date code, not a proven installation date. System original installation is homeowner-reported 1999. Right tank reported ~170 °F and domestic mixed outlet ~105–110 °F are observations, not recommended settings. Both Polaris plates mark 160 °F outlet operation. AM30 maximum inlet is 180 °F. Pressure-reducing valve was not identified along the traced cold feed; absence elsewhere is not proven. Gauge ~65 psi is one uncalibrated snapshot. The 450 psi C26 rating concerns refrigerant. Report source and maintenance Topic Markdown and original photos remain the evidence record. reporting/guide/build.py contains the curated equipment data and SVG geometry; reporting/guide/template.html contains the explanatory narrative and offline interaction code. Changes in findings must update the relevant Markdown and curated guide content before rebuilding. Source chapters are embedded verbatim for offline inspection, with a notice that older entries may be superseded by the synthesis. The guide does not assert live equipment status, live supplier stock, or verified wiring where tracing stopped. External reference links require internet; embedded diagrams and photos do not.

text: Master index Active diagnosis — 2026-11-07 Problem: Upstairs Mix 2 mixed-water circulator does not receive 120 V at DuoMix 201 terminal 8 during upstairs demand, while working first-floor Mix 1 terminal 12 energizes on its call. Wiring breakthrough: ZCM-1 ES brown -> DuoMix 1 (Mix 1 Demand) ; ZCM-2 ES red -> DuoMix 3 (Mix 2 Demand) . DuoMix terminals 2/4 tied . Lower ES other terminal (white) runs to upper radiant zone control module and toward a 24 VAC transformer. ES/ES and OUTPUT are separate terminal groups. Current diagnosis: Both upstairs valves moved open during calls, but their isolated end switches stayed OL. The working Living Room switch changed from OL to continuity. title: Wirsbo DuoMix 201 installation handbook — A3030005 · PDF p. 1
text: A3030005 DuoMix 201 Installation Instructions The WIRSBO DuoMix 201 provides control of two variable speed injection mixing devices in order to satisfy a two temperature system. The system may consist of a two temperature radiant floor heating application, or a combination of snow melting and radiant floor heating. The control is designed for use with radiant systems but can be easily integrated to other hydronic applications (baseboard, fan coil). The control is capable of providing boiler return protection in order to prevent boiler flue gas condensation. The DuoMix 201 includes a large Liquid Crystal Display (LCD) which provides temperature read-out and adjustable settings. For building space heating applications the control includes features such as Warm Weather Shut Down (WWSD), outdoor reset, pump exercising, and maximum supply temperature adjustment. In the snow melting mode the control protects the slab against thermal shock, has idling capabilities, Warm Weather Shut Down (WWSD), and Cold Weather Cut Off (CWCO). Control Strategy OUTDOOR RESET In order to maintain occupant comfort with a hot water heating system, the heat supplied to the building must equal the heat lost by the building. • The heat supplied to a building is proportional to the temperature of the Outdoor Constant Heat Temperature Loss Drop Room Temperature Increase water and the surface of the heating area. A small surface area such as baseboard radiators requires a higher water temperature than a larger surface area such as radiant floors. • The heat supplied to a building/space can be changed by increasing or decreasing the supply water temperature. As the outdoor temperature falls the supply water temperature rises. Theory The calculated heat loss of a building or space is based on the coldest weather conditions the area experiences over the heating season. If the heat demand is analyzed as a percentage of the heating systems capacity, the heating system operates at or near maximum capacity for a small portion of the heating season. If the water temperature is controlled using a non-weather responsive tempering device, shown as the dotted line, the line is flat and does not flucuate with the demand for heat. Resetting the supply water temperature (solid line) allows for the supply water temperature to adjust itself to the demands on the heating system. Lowering the supply water temperature in warmer times of the heating season will allow the radiant zones to be open and run longer, providing increased comfort and efficiency. Water Temperature Optimization The Wirsbo DuoMix 201 uses actual data to program the control on start-up, eliminating the unknowns. Until now, resetting the supply water temperature to a radiant panel meant using terminology such as "curves" and "shifts". The DuoMix now eliminates manually selecting the proper curve based on the design data. From the user inputted data, the control creates a relationship (or ratio) between the outdoor temperature and the water temperature supplied to the radiant application. The control automatically adjusts the supply water temperature for every 1°F drop in outdoor temperature. In order to correctly reset the supply water temperature, a few parameters are required: Outdoor Design Temperature The Outdoor Design Temperature is used to calculate the heat load required at the most severe weather conditions expected during a normal heating season. Design WWSD Supply Temp. 150 Design Supply Water Temperature 60 (15.5) (65) The Design Supply Water Temperature is the temperature of water supplied to the radiant Supply Water Temperature 130 panel(s) to meet the requirements of the heat load calculated at the outdoor design termperature. (54) Design Room Temperature 110 (43) The Design Room Temperature is the indoor air temperature used in the heat loss calculations. Design Room 90 Design (32) Warm Weather Shut Down (WWSD) Temp. Outdoor Temp. When the outdoor air temperature is warmer than the Warm Weather Shut Down setting, no 70 (21) additional heat is supplied to the building; therefore, the heating system can be shut down. text: Indoor Temperature Feedback Most buildings have internal heat gains due to people, passive solar heating and mechanical or electrical equipment. If only the outdoor temperature is measured, the control cannot compensate for these internal heat gains and the building may overheat. In order to prevent overheating, indoor temperature feedback can be combined with the outdoor reset strategy. From this indoor temperature feedback, the control can match the supply water temperature to the heat loss of the building. If the indoor temperature is too warm, the control reduces the supply water temperature, and if the indoor temperature is too cold, the control increases the supply water temperature. SETPOINT OPERATION Some loads, such as pool heating and floor warming, require a low fixed setpoint supply temperature. These loads should be regulated through a mixing device. MIXING OPERATION The full range of water temperatures required through a heating season can be provided with a standard (non-condensing) boiler by incorporating a modulating mixing device into the system. Variable speed injection pumps can modulate both the system supply water temperature and the boiler return water temperature. The full modulation of water temperatures improves comfort in the building and also protects the boiler from cool return water. Boiler Protection Cool water is often returned to the boiler from snow melting or low temperature radiant floor heating systems. This cool boiler return water may cause the boiler to operate at such a low temperature that the flue gases condense. Alternatively, when the boiler surfaces are hot due to previous loads such as domestic hot water generation, the large temperature difference (∆T) between the boiler and its return water can cause the boiler to become thermally shocked. Proper protection of the boiler under these circumstances requires modulating mixing devices that can temporarily reduce the heating load. This is accomplished by reducing the speed of injection pumps. System Maximum Supply Hydronic radiant floor heating systems, usually operate at water temperatures that are below the minimum boiler return temperature. This is due to the large surface area of the floors which radiate a significant amount of heat at low water temperatures. Floor heating systems also have a maximum supply water temperature limit to protect the application in which it is installed. In such systems a mixing device is required to control and limit the supply water temperature to the radiant panel. Sequence of Operation POWERING UP THE CONTROL When the WIRSBO DuoMix 201 is powered up, the words "WIRSBO 201" are displayed for 4 seconds. The control then displays the outdoor temperature and begins normal operation. WARM WEATHER SHUT DOWN (WWSD) When the outdoor temperature rises above the WWSD 1 or WWSD 2 settings, the control shuts off the respective mixing system pump and variable speed injection pump. The WWSD element is displayed whenever both mixing loops are in WWSD. If no heat is required in any mixing system, the boiler enable relay is also turned off. MIXING OPERATION The WIRSBO DuoMix 201 controls the supply water temperature to two different mixing loops (mixing 1 and mixing 2). The control provides the different water temperatures through two separate variable speed injection pump systems. The mixing 1 section can be chosen to operate in setpoint or outdoor reset mode. An optional indoor sensor may be installed in order to obtain indoor temperature feedback. The mixing 2 section can be chosen to operate in setpoint, outdoor reset, or snow melting mode. Outdoor Reset Operation The DuoMix 201 can be used to provide outdoor reset to the mixing loops. The outdoor reset mode (RST) of operation on mixing 1 or mixing 2 must be selected through the display interface. 2 DuoMix Installation Handbook

Indoor Sensor An indoor sensor may be connected to a mixing section in order to obtain indoor temperature feedback. The SENSOR 1 or 2 setting must be set to INDR through the display interface. An external mixing demand is still required in order to provide heat. tekmar Zone Control tekmar Outdoor reset can be combined with zoning. Through Room Temperature Units (RTU), a Zone Control Wirsbo 201 tekmar Zone Control can provide indoor temperature feedback to the WIRSBO 201 control. The 201 will then adjust the supply water temperature to satisfy the zone with the highest water temperature requirement. Heat to the remaining zones will be cycled on and off by the zone control using zone valves or pumps. If a tekmar Zone Control is connected to either the mixing 1 and/or mixing 2 sections, an external demand is not required, although it is still operational for additional zones that are controlled by thermostats. Boiler Enable When heat is required in the heating system the WIRSBO DuoMix 201 turns on the Boiler Enable relay. Once the Boiler Enable relay is turned on, a minimum of 3 minutes is allowed before turning the relay back off if the supply water temperatures are satisfied and the injection pumps have ramped down to 0%. If the heat demand is removed, the boiler is immedi- ately turned off. Boiler Protection A boiler sensor must be installed on the return line to the boiler in order to obtain boiler protection against flue gas condensation, if required. If the boiler return water temperature approaches the boiler minimum setting (Boil RET), the control maintains the Boiler Enable relay on and reduces the speed of the injection pump 2. If the boiler temperature still does not increase, then the speed of injection pump 1, will be decreased. System Maximum Supply The WIRSBO DuoMix 201 has a maximum supply setting (MAX SUP 1 and MAX SUP 2) for each mixing loop, which sets an upper operating limit to the mixed supply water temperatures for the application in which the tubing is installed. This value is different than the Design Supply Setting (DSN SUP1 and DSN SUP2). SETPOINT OPERATION The WIRSBO DuoMix 201 can be used to provide one or two fixed water temperatures to the mixing loops. The setpoint (SETP) mode of operation on mixing 1 or mixing 2 must be selected °F through the display interface. When 24 or 120 V (ac) is applied to the Mix1 Demand terminals, the control turns on the mixing pump 1 (Mix1 Pmp) and operates the variable speed injection pump 1 (Var1 Pmp) in order to supply the adjusted SETPNT 1 water temperature. The mixing 2 section operates in the same manner. SNOW MELTING OPERATION The mixing 2 section on the DuoMix 201 may be used to control a snow melting system. The snow melting mode of operation must be selected through the display interface (SNOW). When the Start button is pressed and held for 1 second on the control or on the Remote Module Unit 040, the control enters the snow melting mode of operation and displays the RUN TIME. The RUN TIME can now be adjusted for the desired operating time. The snow melting can also be enabled by the Remote Snowmelt Enable Kit A3040039. At any time during the snow melting session, the melting time remaining may be viewed. (See View Menu). An external Mix 2 Demand for 4 seconds is equivalent to pressing the Start button. If the Snowmelt Enable Kit is not desired, a Slab Sensor A3060072 and a Universal Sensor A3060071 are required for snow melt operation. DuoMix Installation Handbook 3

text: Caution Improper installation and operation of this control could result in damage to the equipment and possibly even personal injury. It is your responsibility to ensure that this control is safely installed according to all applicable codes and standards. This electronic control is not intended for use as a primary limit control. Other controls that are intended and certified as safety limits must be placed into the control circuit. STEP ONE GETTING READY Check the contents of this package. If any of the contents listed are missing or damaged, please contact your wholesaler or Wirsbo sales representative for assistance. Type 201 includes: • One Wirsbo DuoMix 201 (A3030005) • Three Universal Sensors (A3060071) • One Outdoor Sensor (A3060070) Note Carefully read the Sequence of Operation sections in all applicable brochures to ensure that you have chosen the proper control for your application. STEP TWO MOUNTING THE CONTROL AND SENSORS Installing the Control • Remove the control from its base by pressing down on the release clip in the wiring chamber and sliding the control upwards. • Mount the base directly onto the wall, DIN rail or an electrical box. Installing the Outdoor Sensor A3060070 • Remove the screw and pull the front cover off the sensor enclosure. • The A3060070 can either be mounted directly onto a wall or a 2" x 4" electrical box. When the A3060070 is wall mounted, the wiring should enter through the back or bottom of the enclosure. Do not mount the A3060070 with the conduit knockout facing upwards as rain could enter the enclosure and damage the sensor. • The A3060070 should be mounted on a wall which best represents the heat load on the building (a northern wall for most buildings and a southern facing wall for buildings with large south facing glass areas). The A3060070 should not be exposed to heat sources such as ventilation or window openings. • In order to prevent heat that is transmitted through the wall from affecting the sensor reading, it may be necessary to install an insulating barrier behind the enclosure. • The A3060070 should be installed at an elevation above the ground that will prevent accidental damage or tampering. Installing the Universal Sensor A3060071 • The sensor can be strapped directly to the pipe using the cable tie provided. Insulation should be placed around the sensor to reduce the effect of air currents on the sensor measurement. • The Universal Sensor A3060071 should be placed downstream of a pump or after an elbow or similar fitting. This is especially important if large diameter pipes are used as the thermal stratification within the pipe can result in erroneous sensor readings. Proper sensor location requires that the fluid is thoroughly mixed within the pipe before it reaches the sensor. STEP THREE ROUGH-IN WIRING All electrical wiring terminates in the control base wiring chamber. The base has standard 7/8" (22 mm) knockouts which accept common wiring hardware and conduit fittings. Before removing the knockouts, check the wiring diagram and plan the routing of wires. The control base can be installed on a 4-3/4” x 4-3/4” electrical (dryer or range) box to simplify line voltage wiring. Power must not be applied to any of the wires during the rough-in wiring stage. • Install the Outdoor Sensor , Boiler Return Sensor, and the two Supply Sensors and run the wiring back to the control. • If a 10K Indoor Sensor is used, install the Indoor Sensor(s) according to the installation instructions supplied with the sensor and run the wiring back to the control. • If a tekmar Zone Control is used, run two wires from the Zone Control to the 201. • If a Snow Melt Enable Kit A3040039 or a Remote Display Module 040 is used, run two wires from the unit to the 201. • Run wiring from the other system components (pumps, mix demands, boiler, etc.) to the control. Multi-strand 16 AWG wire is recommended for all 120 V (ac) wiring due to its superior flexibility and ease of installation into the terminals. DuoMix Installation Handbook 5

text: • If required, install the supplied safety dividers between the unpowered sensor inputs and the powered 120 V (ac) or 24 V (ac) wiring chambers. • Do not apply power to the control until the DIP switches are properly set for your application. See the Settings section of this brochure for details on how to set the DIP switches. • Once the settings are complete, apply power to the control. The operation of the control on power up is described in the Sequence of Operation section of this brochure. Settings Before adjusting the control settings, read through the Sequence of Operation section of this brochure to ensure that you understand how the control operates. STEP SIX ESSENTIAL CONTROL SETTINGS Lock- Unlock DIP Switch The Lock-Unlock DIP switch is used to prevent unauthorized persons from tampering with the settings. When the DIP switch is set to Lock ( ) none of the settings may be adjusted. To adjust a setting simply switch the DIP switch to the Unlock ( ) position. Default Settings DIP Switch If the control settings have been erroneously set, the control can be made to operate with factory default Default settings values by switching the Default settings DIP switch. In order to override all current settings with the factory default values, the control must be powered down and powered up with the DIP switch set to Default settings. During normal operation set this DIP switch to Run. Run MODES 1 The MODES 1 adjustment selects the mode of operation for the mixing 1 section. There are three allowable settings: • OFF - If the mixing 1 section is not used, the installer should select this setting. The control assumes the mixing 1 section is not used. All adjustments for the mixing 1 section will be skipped. • RST (reset) - When using the mixing 1 section for building space heating, the installer should select this adjustment. The 201 control operates the mixing 1 section to provide outdoor reset. This is the factory setting. • SETP (setpoint) - When the installer requires a fixed supply water temperature, this setting must be selected. The control operates the mixing 1 section to provide a fixed setpoint temperature equal to the SETPNT 1 temperature adjustment. WWSD 1 WWSD 1 can be adjusted from 35 to 85°F, OFF (2 to 29°C). The mixing 1 section will shut down when the outdoor temperature is warmer than this setting. The WWSD setting also has an effect in the setpoint mode °F of operation. Factory setting is 68°F. SETPNT 1 If setpoint mode of operation is selected, the control operates the variable speed injection pump 1 to provide a setpoint temperature equal to the SETPNT 1 setting. The SETPNT 1 setting can be adjusted from 70 to 200°F °F (21 to 93°C). An external mixing demand on the Mix1 Demand must be present. Factory setting is 110°F. SENSOR 1 The SENSOR 1 adjustment informs the control which external device is connected to the Zo1 / Ind terminal. DSN SUP 2 This setting establishes the design supply water temperature required in order to satisfy the heating system at the design outdoor temperature. This setting is used by the control to calculate the heating curve for the °F mixing 2 section. The DSN SUP 2 setting can be adjusted from 80 to 220°F (27 to 104°C). Factory setting is 110°F. MAX SUP The MAX SUP 2 adjustment is used to set the highest allowable temperature in the mixing 2 section. This setting can be adjusted from 100 to 220°F (38 to 104°C). Factory setting is 180°F. °F MELTING The MELTING setting is the desired slab temperature when snow melting is required. It can be adjusted from 32 to 77°F (0 to 25°C). Factory setting is 36°F. °F IDLING The IDLING setting is the desired slab temperature during idling, and it can be adjusted from 20 to 68°F (-7 to 20°C). If Idling is not desired, this setting must be set to OFF. ∆T MAX The 201 control limits the rate of heat applied to a slab to prevent excessive thermal stress. The rate of heat delivery to the slab is dependant on the difference between the melting system supply and return temperatures. The control measures these temperatures and calculates the difference to give the ∆T. If this °F calculated ∆T approaches the ∆T MAX setting, the control operates the variable speed injection pump to maintain the ∆T at the ∆T MAX setting. The ∆T MAX setting can be adjusted from 10 to 70°F (5 to 39°C). Factory setting is 30°F. CWCO (Cold Weather Cut Off) CWCO is the lowest temperature at which the melting system continues to operate. This temperature is set based on the capacity of the snow melt system and the economics of melting in extreme conditions. The range View Mix 1 Demand Mix 2 Demand °F of this setting is from -20 to 50°F (-29 to 10°C). The CWCO adjustment has an OFF position for systems where Minimum Maximum Melting a minimum outdoor temperature is not a consideration. Idling CWCO RUN TIME The RUN TIME is set to the estimated time required to complete snow melting. This setting may be adjusted from 30 min. to 18 hours. For continuous operation the RUN TIME may be set to INF (infinite). Factory setting is 4 hours. The snow melting run time will start counting down once the slab is up to MELTING temperature. BOILER RETURN To prevent problems of flue gas condensation in the boiler, the Boil RET adjustment is set to the minimum boiler return temperature as specified by the boiler manufacturer. When the boiler return approaches this setting, the control operates the variable speed pump to limit the output until the boiler return can warm up. °F If a minimum boiler return temperature is not required, as with condensing or electric boilers, this adjustment can be set to OFF. This setting can be set from 70 to 180°F (21 to 82°C). Factory setting is 130°F. UNITS (°F - °C) The control can display temperatures in °C or °F. Factory setting is °F. CONTRAST In order to improve visibility of the Liquid Crystal Display (LCD) the CONTRAST of the display may be adjusted. BACKLITE The BACKLITE on the display may be adjusted to OFF, 20 S, or ON. When it is adjusted to 20 S the display is illuminated for 20 seconds after a button is pressed. DuoMix Installation Handbook 11
